evidence.text: Amazon, Astera's lead Scorpio X / Trainium customer and warrant holder, said on 2026-10-29 that its chips business grows at triple-digit percentages year over year, that Trainium and Graviton revenue commitments each rose more than 20x y/y, that prior-generation Trainium capacity sells at a premium to H1, that 2026 cash capex stays ~$220bn, and (per secondary reports) that 2027 capex will be 'meaningfully more'. That is a direct counterparty speaking after Astera last guided (Aug 4) and supports the ~$656m Q4 bar (+19% q/q) and a constructive 2027 tone.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (Aug 4): revenue $392.4m vs $355-365m guide and a Q3 guide of $540-560m far above the ~$410-417m consensus; the stock fell 11.96%. Feb 2026 beat: -21.41%. The name has not paid for strong guides recently.
evidence.why_not_priced: The day after Amazon reported, Astera fell ~11% (2026-10-30) on a sector-wide AI-capex/payback sell-off (Nasdaq -2.9%), so the market traded the macro reading of hyperscaler spend, not the read-through to Astera's lead customer's custom-silicon volumes. If it had been priced as a positive for Astera, the stock would not have under-performed the Nasdaq ~4x on that day and skew would not lean to puts.
evidence.independence: Alphabet held 2026 capex $195-205bn and said capex will 'increase significantly in 2027' (CNBC 2026-10-28, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-googl-earnings-q3-2026.html), a separate counterparty, filed separately as a smaller finding.

evidence.text: Alphabet on 2026-10-28 kept 2026 capex at $195-205bn and its CFO said capex will 'increase significantly in 2027'; Microsoft said calendar-2026 spending ~$170bn with spending accelerating. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable for this line specifically; the stock fell ~11% on 2026-10-30, the day after these capex statements, so the macro reading has recently been negative.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is wire copy and the sector sold off on it (Alphabet -10% on search). Filed because the 2027 capex direction is the one input the Q4/2027 tone depends on, and Astera's own price has moved as if 2027 spend were at risk (Northland's Oct 9 downgrade thesis).
evidence.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission, not a statement about Astera. Different document from the Amazon finding. evidence.text: Astera has fallen after each of its last three revenue beats: Feb 2026 -21.41%, May 2026 -0.83%, Aug 2026 -11.96% (the last on a Q3 guide ~30% above consensus); 2 of 7 prints since IPO-era coverage rose. Q3 is guided to the consensus midpoint ($550m), so a beat to ~$575-590m is expected, and the reaction turns on the Q4 guide versus ~$656m and gross margin versus ~72%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: -11.96, -0.83, -21.41, +1.47, +28.66, -0.38, -10.89; median |move| 10.89. Beats sold three times running.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pattern is public, but the whisper EPS ($1.30) above the top of the guide shows the buy-side still expects a beat-and-raise; if the beat-and-sell pattern were fully priced the whisper would sit at guide and options would not still carry an 11.6% event move with a put skew.
evidence.independence: Baseline history (8-K item 2.02 acceptance times) confirms the same moves from a different source; same underlying facts, so one finding.

evidence.text: The stock has de-rated hard into the print: -38.3% over 20 sessions and -16.1% over 5, 50% below its 52-week high, at ~46x forward earnings against a one-year average of 72x and a March low of 41x, with no company-specific negative news (falls attributed to the FT OpenAI-revenue report on Oct 8, the Northland/Citi downgrades on Oct 9, and the Oct 30 AI sell-off). The bar for the reaction is lower than in August, when the stock sat near $340-400.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2025, after a weak spell, the stock rose +28.66% on a beat-and-raise; the three most recent prints came after strong run-ups and fell.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced by definition (it is the price). What is not visible: if the market expected a weak Q4 guide on company-level evidence, there would be a company-level trigger; none exists in the record, and the drawdown tracks sector moves. Against this, skew of +6.2 says the option market still pays for downside, so the size is held small.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d -38.3%, pct_from_52w_high -50.2%) confirms the drawdown; Earnings Whispers/finviz 2026-10-26 notes sentiment moved from slightly bearish to near neutral (https://finviz.com/news/408291/astera-labs-must-prove-its-40-scorpio-driven-revenue-leap-as-shares-sink-toward-lows).

evidence.text: Gross margin is falling: non-GAAP GM 76.4% in Q1, 73.7% in Q2, guided ~72% for Q3, with ~200bp a quarter from the non-cash Amazon warrant contra-revenue and the rest from lower-margin hardware modules; consensus 2026 GM 72.6% and 2027 70.9%. As Amazon's purchases scale (chips triple-digit growth), warrant vesting grows, so a Q4 GM guide below ~72% is a plausible negative inside the reported structure.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM 73.7% (down from 76.4%) came with the -11.96% reaction, though the guide was strong; margin is the line commentators name as the real test.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly inside what the company guided (72% for Q3) and in consensus (70.9% for 2027); the unpriced part is only whether Q4 steps lower as the warrant vests faster, which no preview quantifies.
evidence.independence: Q2 8-K ex 99.1 gives the ~72% GM outlook (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001736297/000173629726000033/q226exhibit991.htm). Inference about Q4 is mine.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced and pre-planned (10b5-1); the only residual is a supply overhang into any post-print rally once the window opens. Small for that reason.

first_hunter_context.bar: Company guide: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA $850M-$1.0B, reiterated on the Q2 call 2026-07-29 (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/CAR-2Q26-AI-Summary; raised from $800M-1B on Q1, https://rallies.ai/news/avis-posts-70-first-quarter-utilization-record-raises-2026-ebitda-outlook), with Q3 guided to roughly flat RPD and an Americas fleet down mid-single digits. Q3 EPS consensus is disputed: Benzinga $8.34 non-GAAP vs another aggregator $8.5951 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAR/earnings-forecasts, via search 2026-11-03); no Q3 revenue or EBITDA consensus found. The guide is sourced, the quarterly bar is not, so the reported-quarter findings are capped small. Arithmetic: H1 2026 adj EBITDA = -113 + 286 = $173M (Q1 and Q2 releases), so H2 must deliver $677-827M against H2 2025 of $564M (Q3 559 + Q4 5, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361226000010/a03-prxpressreleasexq4f25.htm).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: FINRA settlement 2026-09-30: 5.25M shares short, 11.0 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/car); Equibles model for 2026-10-15 ~5.41M (estimate, not reported: https://equibles.com/stocks/car/short-interest). Shares outstanding 35,325,754 at 2026-07-22 (Q2 10-Q cover), so ~15% of shares outstanding; the free float is much smaller because Pentwater (>19-22%) and other holders lock up a large block (April 2026 squeeze reports: 54% of free float short, https://rallies.ai/news/avis-budget-shares-surge-340-on-short-squeeze-atm-offering-to-raise-2b), so the short is crowded against the tradable float. Skew +8.3 vol points (25d put over call): downside is being paid. Put/call OI 0.68, total OI only 1,356 and ATM spread 54% of mid, so the option read is thin. Run-up +9.07% over 5 sessions (+6.3% on 2026-10-30 with no news found), -1.04% over 20, -84% off the 52w high from the squeeze.

evidence.text: Holding the reiterated FY2026 adj EBITDA guide of $850M-$1.0B requires H2 of $677-827M, +20% to +47% over H2 2025's $564M, while management guided Q3 RPD roughly flat and the Americas fleet down mid-single digits, and said forward bookings had eroded since early May; a guide cut toward or below $850M is the live risk on the line this stock trades on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print with a ~$150M Q4 shortfall vs guide and a $800M-1B first guide: -21.54%. Jul 2025 (-15.41%) and Jul 2026 (-6.9%, guide reiterated but demand softer) both fell. Q1 2026 guide raise to $850M-1B still fell 18% on a wider loss per chartmill, though the baseline's close-to-close shows -0.47%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the disputed EPS consensus ($8.34, below Q3 2025's level) suggests the Street already sits near or below the low end of the guide, and the put skew pays for downside. If a cut were fully priced, the stock would not have run +9% in five sessions into the print and consensus would sit openly below the guide-implied Q3; neither is visible.
evidence.independence: H1 actuals from the company's own Q1 and Q2 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000072361226000037/a03-pressreleasexq2f26.htm) and the Q4 2025 release for the H2 2025 base; the demand softening is echoed by an Auto Rental News headline of 2026-08-02, 'Avis Cuts Fleet as Summer Demand Trails Expectations' (headline only). The TSA and Manheim findings below are separate series feeding this same guide risk and are sized for their own quarter effect only.

evidence.text: TSA checkpoint volumes for 21 Jun-7 Sep 2026 were 204.15M against 209.91M in 2025 (-2.7%), August -4.4%; early September was flat (+0.2%). Airport rental days fall with them; Avis had already guided the fleet down mid-single digits for Q3, so most of this sits inside the guide.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09 (article covers through 2026-09-07; page returned 403, figures from search snippet, snippet_only)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rental-day/volume shortfalls fed the Feb 2026 (-21.54%) and Jul 2026 (-6.9%) declines; no isolated read for volume alone.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: TSA data is public daily and the company pre-guided a smaller fleet. If the market saw volumes worse than guided, consensus would show visible downward revisions after September; I found none dated.
evidence.independence: https://deeparrival.com/news/tsa-summer-checkpoint-traveler-volume-drop-2026/ (same TSA series, separate tally). Proxy, not company-confirmed; Hertz guided Q3 transaction days +~1%, which cuts the other way.

evidence.text: The Manheim used-vehicle index fell to 205.9 in September 2026, -0.6% y/y and -1.1% m/m, its first reading below year-ago in 2026, with SUV values pressured partly by younger rental-fleet supply; mid-October recovered to 207.4 (+2.2% y/y). That is a slight headwind to Q3 gains on sale and DPU, and neutral-to-positive for Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Higher depreciation and lower gains on sale were $60M of the ~$150M Q4 2025 shortfall, which drove the -21.54% reaction in Feb 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: A public series the sell side tracks, so mostly priced; the size of the September dip is small and the October rebound already offsets it.
evidence.independence: Mid-October reading 207.4 (+2.2% y/y) from Cox Automotive's Oct 2026 mid-month report, https://www.coxautoinc.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/October-2026-Mid-Month-Market-Insights.pdf (via search snippet; PDF unreadable).

evidence.text: Hertz, the direct peer, spoke after Avis (2026-08-06): Q2 RPD +9% and RPU +8% on 'a more balanced industry supply-demand environment', a small World Cup benefit, 'forward views on residual values remain stable', and Q3 adj corporate EBITDA guided at $275-325M with transaction days up ~1%. That is a more constructive industry pricing read than Avis's own flat-RPD Q3 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of CAR reacting to an RPD surprise in the baseline; Q1 2026's +3% RPD beat came with an -0.47% close-to-close reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Three months old and public. The part that may not be priced is that Avis guided RPD flat on 2026-07-29 before Hertz described a firmer industry; if the market had taken that read, CAR would not trade at a flat-RPD-implied consensus below last year. Hertz's own Q3 print is 2026-11-05, after this window.
evidence.independence: Hertz Q3 guidance $275-325M and transaction days ~+1% also via https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2972207/hertz-global-stock-rises-124-since-q2-earnings-release. Partly Hertz-specific (its own fleet-rotation turnaround), so the transmission to Avis pricing is a proxy.

evidence.text: Short interest is 5.25M shares (2026-09-30 settlement) with 11.0 days to cover on ~394k average daily volume, against a free float much smaller than the 35.3M shares outstanding; any print that holds the guide forces cover into thin turnover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same crowded short did not prevent -6.9% (Jul 2026) or -21.54% (Feb 2026) on weak guides; it fed the April 2026 squeeze outside earnings. So the squeeze needs a non-negative print to act.
evidence.why_not_priced: The +9% five-day run-up into the print may be early covering, so partly priced. If the squeeze risk were fully priced, call skew would be bid relative to puts; instead the 25d skew is +8.3 toward puts.
evidence.independence: Equibles model for the 2026-10-15 settlement ~5.41M (rising): https://equibles.com/stocks/car/short-interest. Aug 14 settlement 5.4M at 15.8 DTC: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/car/short-interest/.

evidence.text: Avis received the $650M Pentwater Section 16(b) settlement in cash on 2026-10-05 (about $18 a share, ~16% of the ~$3.9B market cap), to be recognized in Q4, and on 2026-11-02 gave notice to redeem the remaining $350M of 5.75% notes due 2027 at par on 2026-12-30. Net corporate leverage was 7.4x against a target of at least one turn lower by year-end, so the call may give a pro forma leverage number or a use for the ~$300M remainder.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The settlement announcement produced a +5.22% overnight rise (https://www.itiger.com/news/1104931090); the baseline carries no print reaction on a balance-sheet item.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both 8-Ks are public. What is not public is any use of the remaining ~$300M (deleveraging vs buyback); a buyback on a tiny float with 11 days of short would be visible as upside, but nothing says one is coming. Below operating income and outside adjusted EBITDA, so sized as a fraction.
evidence.independence: Redemption notice 8-K 2026-11-02: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000095014226002911/eh260848006_8k.htm (same programme, same company; one fact chain).

evidence.text: On 2026-09-21 Avis closed a $650M five-year AESOP Series 2026-5 fleet ABS (Class A $474.5M at 5.69%, Class D at 8.14%): routine fleet financing with market access intact, no stated distress use.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public 8-K, a routine fleet-funding renewal. What the money buys: vehicles for the domestic fleet, consistent with a fleet held down mid-single digits rather than a ramp. Signed zero after asking.
evidence.independence: Q2 10-Q: $1,867M vehicle-program capacity available, covenants in compliance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000072361226000039/car-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: Wayfair has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last seven quarters, by $0.02B to $0.16B (Q2 2026: $3.52B vs $3.47B). The Q3 guide of high-single-digit growth on a $3,117M base implies about $3.37-3.40B, and the CEO wrote on 2026-08-04 that he expects 'even further acceleration' beyond Q2's 7.5%. Against MarketBeat's $3.38B bar a modest revenue beat is the base case; against Chartmill's $3.442B (+10.4%) it would be an in-line print or a slight miss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beat in all seven quarters, yet the stock fell -13.02% on 2026-02-19 and -12.75% on 2026-04-30. Q1 2026 was a revenue beat with an EPS miss and negative FCF (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1617713/wayfairs-nysew-q1-cy2026-beats-on-revenue-but-stock-drops). It rose +29.97% on 2026-08-04 and +23.22% on 2025-10-28 when the beat came with EBITDA and FCF strength. Revenue alone has not set the sign.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. A seven-quarter beat streak is visible on every terminal, and the 10.4%-growth estimate already embeds a beat over the guide. If the market expected an outsized revenue beat, the skew would lean to calls; it is flat at +0.22.
evidence.independence: Company 8-K for Q2 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001616707/000161670726000147/a2026-08x04ex991.htm): US revenue +8.7%, orders +6.0%, active customers +3.3%, Q2 orders up 12% sequentially. This is the company's own document, separate from the estimate aggregator.

evidence.text: Third-party data for the category softened through Q3. The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor, on a new card-panel methodology, shows furniture and home furnishings sales down 2.7% YoY in September 2026, the only major category to decline. NAR shows August existing-home sales at a two-year low and September at 3.99M SAAR, down YoY in all four regions. Wayfair's growth therefore rests entirely on share gains (it cites a 'high single digit share spread').
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wayfair rose +30% in Aug 2026 and +23% in Oct 2025 while the category was weak, because the company said its guide assumed no recovery. Category weakness has not hurt the print when share gains held. The Q1 2026 drop (-12.75%) came with 'choppy demand' commentary.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Both series are public, and Wayfair's Q3 guide already assumed no category recovery. What may not be priced is the Q4 guide: a September category that is negative YoY, with housing at a two-year low, makes it harder to guide holiday growth above Q3. If the market had priced a soft Q4 guide, the 20-day run-up of +5.4% and a stock near its 52-week high would look different.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Housing data from NAR via Mortgage News Daily (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/news/10162026-existing-home-sales-nar-inventory-prices-appr) points the same way. RH guided Q3 revenue +5-6% on 2026-09-10 (https://pulse2.com/rh-q2-revenue-rises-2-6-to-922-2-million-as-company-targets-up-to-7-fiscal-2026-growth/amp/), a slow but positive high-end read.

EBITDA margin was guided to 6-7%, against 6.9% in Q2 2026 and 6.7% in Q3 2025. The guide leaves little room for margin expansion year over year in Q3, and margin is the line the stock has traded on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin and profit drove the large moves: Q1 2026 EPS miss and negative FCF, -12.75%; Q2 2026 EBITDA +18% with record FCF, +29.97%; Q3 2025 EBITDA $208M vs $119M, +23.22%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The comment is inside the company's own guide, and the consensus EPS of $0.77-0.80 vs $0.70 last year already sits inside it. This is filed because the margin line is where this stock's sign has come from, not because the market has missed it.
